# magpie-ima-auth English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) Signs in to **ima** (腾讯 ima.copilot, `ima.qq.com`) — the AI knowledge workbench — and puts its models in front of an agent, drawn on that account's own 算力. One provider, `ima`. magpie has no built-in for it, so an agent set to `ima/` talks to ima directly. > **Not official.** This is a third-party plugin. ima and ima.copilot belong to > Tencent; this repository is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. It works > by calling endpoints that ima publishes to no one — they can change or vanish > without notice, and this will break when they do. Your credentials are yours: > the plugin sends them only to `ima.qq.com`, stores them in OpenCode's or > magpie's own auth file, and nothing here phones home. ## What ima is, and why this plugin is a bridge ima has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and this plugin does not pretend otherwise. Three of its facts shape everything: 1. **It is session-based and takes ONE question.** There is no messages array to send. A conversation is opened first: ```http POST /cgi-bin/session_logic/init_session {"env_info":{"interact_type":2,"robot_type":10000},"name":"…","msgs_limit":20} → {"code":0,"session_id":"…"} ``` and each turn is then asked on its own: ```http POST /cgi-bin/assistant/qa (SSE) {"session_id":"…","robot_type":10000,"question":"…","question_type":2, "client_id":"","model_info":{"model_type":3,"model_id":"official_3"}} ``` So this plugin keeps **one ima session per agent conversation**, flattens the client's messages into the single question ima takes, and translates ima's SSE back into `chat.completion` chunks. 2. **Models are a `(type, id)` pair, not a name.** `deepseek-v4-flash` is `model_type: 3` and `model_id: "official_3"`. Nothing in the request is ever the model's name. 3. **Business errors hide inside HTTP 200.** A login past its end is `code 41`, a refused one `600001`, a spent session `5` or `51` — all in the body of a `200`. Judging by status code alone makes a dead account look alive, so the stream is read to its `COMPLETED` / `INNER_EXCEPTION` sentinel and that is what decides. ## Signing in ima has no authorization page to send a browser to and no token endpoint to poll, so there is **no automatic sign-in** like WorkBuddy's. Two ways in: ### Account (cookie) — the reliable one 1. Sign in to and send ima any message. 2. DevTools (F12) → **Network** → click the request to `/cgi-bin/assistant/qa` → **Request Headers**. 3. Copy the whole value of the **`x-ima-cookie`** header and paste it into magpie. > **It must be that header's value, not the browser's cookie store.** ima's > frontend puts fields in that header that never appear in the cookie store, > and a store-only rebuild is answered with `600001 服务繁忙`. The plugin tells > you this, because the failure otherwise looks like ima being busy. ### ima desktop's sign-in — removed There used to be a second sign-in that read the account the ima desktop app was signed in to, out of the app's own Chromium cookie store (decrypted under the logged-in user's key — DPAPI on Windows). **It does not work, and it was removed rather than shipped as a choice that fails.** What was measured: - The store is found and the tokens decrypt. That part was fine. - **ima never writes a signed-in session to disk.** The Extension Cookies store holds five of the eleven fields ima's client assembles into an `x-ima-cookie`, and a search of every file under the profile for the token value — plain and base64 — finds nothing. The session lives in the running process's memory. - The five fields it does hold are the ones from *before* the last sign-out. Signing in again rewrites `IMA-GUID` and leaves both tokens byte-for-byte the same length, and ima answers them `code 41` / `110031 token session expired`. The refresh endpoint rejects them too. - Getting the full eleven fields needs the running client's cookies, which means a debugging port. ima ignores `--remote-debugging-port` — the flag reaches the main process's command line and nothing ever listens. So the option could only ever fail, and a user picking it would have no way to tell why. The pasted cookie is the whole of what works. The store is still worth writing down for whoever looks next: ima's login lives in `Extension Cookies` and not in `Default/Network/Cookies`, which holds a few hundred advertising cookies and none of ima's. ``` %LOCALAPPDATA%\ima.copilot\User Data\Default\Extension Cookies ← the login %LOCALAPPDATA%\ima.copilot\User Data\Default\Network\Cookies ← ad cookies, none of ima's ``` While ima is running, neither store can be read — Chromium holds them with a lock that `copyFileSync`, `readFileSync`, a hand-rolled `openSync`/`readSync` loop, `[System.IO.File]::Open` with `FileShare.ReadWrite`, `esentutl /y` and `sqlite3` with `immutable=1` were all measured against, and none of them got past it. ## Where the sign-in is kept As an OpenCode `oauth` auth: the `IMA-TOKEN` as `access`, the `IMA-REFRESH-TOKEN` as `refresh`, the token's end, the account, and the whole cookie under `cookie` (ima needs several of its fields at once, and OpenCode's auth shape has no way to name them). OpenCode keeps it in `auth.json`; magpie in `plugin-auth.json`. ## Tokens ima's token lives about two hours and is renewed at `POST /auth_login/refresh` with `{refresh_token, user_id, registration_id}`. **The sign-in renews itself.** Paste the cookie once; magpie calls `auth.refresh` on a schedule and the plugin spends the refresh token, saving back what changed. `auth.usage` renews too before it reads, so a card refreshed by hand recovers on its own rather than waiting for a background pass. ima's refresh tokens rotate — the second refresh of a pair is answered with a dead one — so concurrent renewals are single-flighted per account. Two things this depends on, both of which were wrong before and are the reason an earlier version asked for the cookie every two hours: - **The stored record's `expires` has to be carried through.** `fromAuth` used to drop it, and the check that decides whether to renew asked a freshly built object instead of the sign-in, so a record without it was treated as "not due" and never renewed. - **A record with no `expires` is renewed on a timer, not assumed fresh.** There is no schedule to renew on, so the alternative is using the token until ima refuses it — which is how the card ends up saying "unavailable" hours after the sign-in quietly died. A renewal that fails returns nothing rather than throwing: magpie treats a throw from `auth.refresh` as fatal, and a token with time left on it should not be brought down by a renewal that did not work. **ima rotates the refresh token** — a renewal spends the old one. Two concurrent renewals of one account leave the second holding a dead token, and every request after it fails `600001` until the account is signed in again. Renewals are therefore single-flighted, keyed by account and refresh token. This is a correctness requirement, not an optimisation. magpie (with `refreshLead`) renews ahead of time, once per account, before its requests and model list. The check inside the loader stays for OpenCode, which doesn't call `auth.refresh`. A renewal that fails leaves the current token in use while it lasts, and says so once per account rather than on every request. ## Requests One agent conversation = one ima session, kept 30 minutes and identified by the session magpie names (its `chat.headers` hook), else the chat's first user message. - The chat's instructions (system and developer messages) ride on the **first** question of a session: ima has no system role, and repeating an agent's whole system prompt on every turn of a long session would spend most of the window on it. Verified: an instruction to answer in under 15 characters is obeyed. - Text events are **deltas**, not the answer so far, and are concatenated. Verified over a 29-event answer. - A thinking model sends its reasoning as its own block — `{"Type":"blockThinking","Data":{"thinking_message":{"Message":…}}}` — also a delta stream, but under `Message` where the answer uses `Text`. It goes to `reasoning_content`, never into `content`. - `SUGGEST_QUESTION`, which ima sends after every answer, is a **list** of suggestions whose items each carry a `Text`. It is not the answer, and must not be read as one. - ima states a 20-message session limit (`msgs_limit: 20` is what the frontend sends) but **does not enforce it**: a session accepted 13 turns, 26 messages, without complaint. So this plugin does not rotate at that limit — rotating there would throw away live context for nothing. The code 5 / 51 recovery is what handles a session ima really has finished, and a far-backstop rotation at 60 messages is all that runs unasked. - Images and other non-text parts become `[an image, which this model can't see]` rather than vanishing — a message that silently loses its figure reads to the model as a question about nothing. ## Two chats, one endpoint ima has two different conversations on the same account, and they share an endpoint but nothing else. Which one a turn belongs to is decided by three request fields, all measured against a real account: | | knowledge base Q&A | **copilot** | |---|---|---| | endpoint | `/cgi-bin/assistant/qa` | `/cgi-bin/assistant/qa` | | `robot_type` | `10000` | **`15`** | | `command_info` | `{question_info:{}}` | **`{type:2000, copilot_qa_info:{}}`** | | `model_type` | 3 / 0 / 1001 / 3000 | **`110000`** (`OfficialPaid`) | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | **`text/plain;charset=UTF-8`** | | charged at | free Q&A | **算力**, at a per-model rate | Neither is encrypted. The `/cgi-bin/s/` secure channel — with its `x-ima-cm` / `x-ima-ckey` / `x-ima-ctk` headers and a native `EncryptData` that only the desktop client can run — applies to some *other* endpoints, not to either chat. Model ids are namespaced `copilot/…` versus bare, because the same model is a different ima model on each robot: Hy3 is `official_0` in the knowledge base (free) and `official_paid_hy3` in copilot (charged at ×0.2). A custom model — one the user added with their own API key — is the same on both, so it is listed once, bare. ## Models ### copilot — charged at 算力 Read from `/cgi-bin/model_manage/get_models` with **`{"scene":1}`**. The ids are per-account (`official_paid_ep-i2azx8ko` is *this* account's DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), so this table cannot be static — it is asked for after signing in. The multiplier comes back in `model_token_copywriting`. | Model id | Name | 算力 | |---|---|---| | `copilot/auto` | 自动选择最优模型 | ×1.0 | | `copilot/hy3` | Hy3 | ×0.2 | | `copilot/hy4-preview` | Hy4 preview | ×0.9 | | `copilot/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | ×0.2 闲时 | | `copilot/mimo-v2.6-flash` | MiMo-V2.6-Flash | ×0.2 | | `copilot/mimo-v2.6-pro` | MiMo-V2.6-Pro | ×0.6 | | `copilot/minimax-m3` | MiniMax-M3 | ×0.6 | | `copilot/glm-5.3-flash` | GLM-5.3-Flash | ×0.2 | | `copilot/glm-5.3` | GLM-5.3 | ×2.2 | | `copilot/kimi-k2.7-code` | Kimi-K2.7-Code | ×1.9 | | `copilot/kimi-k2.8-preview` | Kimi-K2.8-Preview | ×1.9 | | `copilot/kimi-k3` | Kimi-K3 | ×4.5 | The spread is 22×, which makes the rate the most consequential thing about choosing one. Kimi-K3 at ×4.5 costs as much as twenty-three Hy3 turns. Note that `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (copilot) and `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (knowledge base, `official_3`) are different models. ### knowledge base — free Read from the same endpoint with `{}`. Thinking variants come off `sub_model_infos`, keyed `"1"` — **the key is not the model_type** (DeepSeek's plain is type 3 and its thinking type 1), so the pair is read out of the sub-model. `enable_thinking` is `false` on every one ima returns, including ones that demonstrably think, so it is not read. | Model id | Name | ima's `(type, id)` | |---|---|---| | `deepseek-v4-flash` | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | `3`, `official_3` | | `deepseek-v4-flash-think` | DeepSeek-V4-Flash (think) | `1`, `official_1` | | `hy4-preview` | Hy4 preview | `1001`, `official_1001` | | `hy4-preview-think` | Hy4 preview (think) | `1002`, `official_1002` | | `hy3` | Hy3 | `0`, `official_0` | | `hy3-think` | Hy3 (think) | `2`, `official_2` | | `glm-5.3-flash` | GLM-5.3-Flash | `3000`, `official_3000` | | `glm-5.3-flash-think` | GLM-5.3-Flash (think) | `3001`, `official_3001` | ### custom — the account's own `model_type: 1000000`, a UUID for an id, `describe: "自定义模型"`. These are models the user connected with their own API key; ima charges no 算力 for them, so they carry no rate. Their names are already ids (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `kimi-k2.6`), and they answer on either robot. **The cookie is sent exactly as signed in.** An earlier version stripped `CLIENT-TYPE` from the catalogue request, on a misread ablation, and it made things strictly worse: with the field, `{}` answers with four official models plus all five customs and `{"scene":1}` with the twelve copilot models plus the same five; without it, `{}` answers with four and no customs, and `{"scene":1}` with six — losing every `official_paid_*` and leaving `official_100000` named "默认模型" instead of "自动选择最优模型". ima reports no context window in either catalogue, so the numbers in the table are this package's own and should be believed least. ## Not supported **Tools.** ima's Q&A endpoint takes one question string. The knowledge base's chat has no tool channel at all, and while copilot's *client* sends a `client_tools` list, the endpoint behind it still takes a single question — there is no tool-call turn to send a result back on. The plugin sends an empty list and declares every model as taking no tools, rather than pretending otherwise. (Trae's package emulates tools by writing the schema into a prompt and parsing tagged blocks back out; that was left out here on purpose — it is a large parser resting on models that were never trained to emit the tags.) Also missing, and not guessed at: - **Knowledge-base targeting.** ima's Q&A runs against whatever the session was opened with; this plugin opens plain sessions, not ones scoped to a knowledge base id. ## 算力 and the daily login `auth.usage` reports what is left of the account's 算力: ```js { balance: "279.4 算力", user: "", windows: [] } ``` `display_amount` on the wire is the figure ima itself shows and is what `balance` carries; the `balance` field on the wire is the same number truncated. Both arrive as strings at the *top level* of the envelope, not under `data`. ima publishes no rate-limit window, so `windows` stays empty rather than carrying an invented one — the allowance *is* the balance, and magpie renders it verbatim under "what is left on the account besides its windows". ### The daily login reward is not implemented ima pays 50 算力 for logging in on the day, and there is a `/cgi-bin/daily_login_activity/check_in` that claims it. **It cannot be called from outside ima's own client**, measured on a day the app itself reported as claimable (`status: 3`, `button: "签到"`): - The route exists — it answers 403, where every wrong name under the same prefix answers 404 (`claim_reward`, `share`, `sign`, `reward` …). - It refuses every body: `{}`, `reward_type` 0–20, `day`, `date`, `top`. - It refuses every header: with or without `x-ima-uid`, `x-ima-token`, `sec-fetch-*`; and as `text/plain`, form-encoded, or with no content type. - Under `/cgi-bin/s/` — the encrypted prefix — it is a 404. - The code that calls it appears in **none** of ima's 1663 extension bundles, so the request shape cannot be read off it either. - The one route that would let a request be encrypted is the client's own debugging port, which ima no longer opens: `--remote-debugging-port` reaches the main process's command line and nothing ever listens. So `auth.checkin` is not exported. magpie would otherwise show a Daily check-in row that failed every day with no way for the user to act on it — the same reasoning as the desktop sign-in below. Reading the day list still works, if you want the streak: `/cgi-bin/daily_login_activity/get_activity_info` answers with a row per day, each carrying `top`, `status`, `reward` and — usefully — `button`, which says what the app would do (`签到`, `已领取`, `已过期`). ## Use In magpie, from **设置 → 插件** (Plugins): paste any one of these into the box marked *"已有想装的？"* and press 安装 — ``` github:dongsujiang0205-coder/magpie-ima-auth from GitHub D:\path\to\magpie-ima-auth a folder on this machine magpie-ima-auth from npm, once published ``` — or from a terminal, if magpie is on your PATH: ```sh magpie plugin add github:dongsujiang0205-coder/magpie-ima-auth magpie plugin login ima ``` `plugin login ima` prints the cookie instructions below and waits for the value to be pasted. OpenCode, in `opencode.json`: ```json { "plugin": ["magpie-ima-auth"] } ``` then `opencode auth login`. ## Checking it ```sh npm test # 45 tests, including an end-to-end turn against a fake ima node smoke.mjs # 10 checks: every hook magpie calls, in magpie's own shapes $env:IMA_COOKIE = "..." # the x-ima-cookie header's own value, from a real ima npm run verify:live # the plugin's own code, against real ima npm run verify:quota # the 算力 balance, through auth.usage npm run scan # nothing identifying in what this repository ships ``` The tests run a real HTTP server that speaks ima's session + SSE shape (`IMA_HOST` points the plugin at it), so the bridge is exercised for what it is — translating between two wire formats — rather than mocked at the seams. `verify-live.mjs` re-runs the whole thing against a real account: the model catalogue, a non-streaming turn with instructions, a streaming turn on a thinking model, three turns of one conversation (asking it to recall a number and then do arithmetic on it, which only works if the session is real), and an unknown model id. It asks real questions and leaves them in the account's ima history, and it never calls `/auth_login/refresh`. `read-magpie-binary.mjs` is how magpie's plugin contract was read rather than guessed: it pulls the readable text around a needle out of magpie's Bun single-file executable, and the comments on `auth.usage` / `auth.checkin` there are what this plugin answers in. Pass it the path to your magpie binary: ```sh node scripts/read-magpie-binary.mjs "" auth.usage ``` `scan-personal.mjs` is what you run before publishing a fork: it checks every file the repository ships for a credential, a device fingerprint, a Windows profile name or an opaque secret. ## Where the protocol comes from Everything above marked "measured" was run against a real account with the tools in `scripts/`. The rest was cross-checked against two independent implementations that agree on it: - [`chipchipss/buddyhub`](https://github.com/chipchipss/buddyhub) — Go, a running gateway (`internal/extprovider/ima/`), whose notes say it was ported from `ima2api`. - [`whynpc9/opencli-plugin-ima`](https://github.com/whynpc9/opencli-plugin-ima) — Node, documents the same headers, and records the `600001` that a store-rebuilt cookie gets. That was confirmed by accident here: a hand-pasted browser cookie jar carries **no** `IMA-*` field at all. Where those two disagreed with a real account, the account won, and it won often: - `official_3000` is GLM-5.3-Flash, not the GLM-5.2 both tables call it. - `models` is at the top level of the catalogue answer, not in a `data` envelope. - The 20-message session limit is not enforced. - **The copilot models are not in either implementation**, because both target the knowledge base's Q&A. copilot is `robot_type: 15` on the same endpoint with a different `command_info`, and it has twelve models those tables never mention, including one account has no name for: the ids are per-account. - `/cgi-bin/s/` and its `EncryptData` turn out to have nothing to do with either chat. The reverse-engineering of them was a wrong turn taken because the two implementations' notes were followed instead of asking ima. ## Releasing Every pushed change is a version. The version in `package.json` marks the state a release describes, and a `v*` tag marks the commit it was cut from. ```sh # 1. decide the version: patch for a fix, minor for a feature, # major when the plugin's contract with magpie changes npm version patch # 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1 (also commits and tags) # 2. push the commit and the tag together git push origin main --tags # 3. publish to npm npm publish ``` Tagging matters more than it looks: magpie's `magpie plugin update` installs the newest version of each plugin, and a tag is what says which commit that is. Commits between two tags are development — the version number only ever moves when a release is being cut, which is why several commits can share one version. Releases are also on GitHub: **Releases → Create a new release** → pick the tag you just pushed. ### Where the icon and the summary come from magpie reads those two from different places depending on how a plugin is installed: | Source | Icon | Summary | | --- | --- | --- | | npm package | `package.json` `icon` | `package.json` `description` | | Official marketplace | shipped with the listing | shipped with the listing | | GitHub repository | the repository API's `icon` field | the repository's Description | GitHub's repository API returns no `icon` field for a **personal account**, so a plugin installed from GitHub always gets the generic glyph. Owning the icon therefore means publishing to npm, which is also why `icon` is an absolute URL pinned to the release tag: npm has to be able to fetch it, and a relative `icon.png` will not resolve. The GitHub-sourced summary just needs a Description filled in, through the gear next to About on the repository page. ## License MIT

# magpie-ima-auth [English](README.md) | **简体中文** 登录 **ima**（腾讯 ima.copilot，`ima.qq.com`）——AI 知识工作台——并把它账号下的 模型交给 Agent 使用，消耗的是该账号自己的**算力**。 一个 provider，id 是 `ima`。magpie 没有内置，所以 Agent 里设成 `ima/<模型名>` 就直接连 ima。 > **非官方。** 本项目是第三方插件。ima 和 ima.copilot 属于腾讯，与腾讯无隶属 > 或背书关系。它靠调用 ima 未公开的接口工作——这些接口可能随时变化或消失， > 届时本插件会失效。你的凭据归你自己：插件只把它们发往 `ima.qq.com`，存在 > OpenCode 或 magpie 自己的 auth 文件里，这里没有任何东西回传。 ## 这个插件在做什么 ima 没有 OpenAI 兼容接口，本插件也不假装有。它做了三件事： 1. **用一个 ima 会话对应一段 Agent 对话。** ima 的接口每次只收一个字符串， 没有 messages 数组。插件把客户端的整段对话压成那一个问题，再把 ima 返回的 SSE 翻译成 `chat.completion` 的流式分片。 2. **模型是 `(type, id)` 二元组，不是名字。** 例如 `deepseek-v4-flash` 对应 `model_type: 3` + `model_id: "official_3"`。 3. **业务错误藏在 HTTP 200 里。** 登录过期是 `code 41`，被拒绝是 `600001`， 会话失效是 `5` 或 `51`——全都在 200 的 body 里。只看状态码会让一个死账号 看起来还活着。 协议细节（字段、错误码、模型 ID）见 [English 版](README.md)，那边是完整的。 ## 登录 ima 没有授权页可以跳转，也没有 token 端点可以轮询，所以**没有自动登录**。 两种方式： ### 粘贴 cookie（唯一可靠的方式） 1. 浏览器打开 登录，给 ima 发任意一条消息。 2. F12 → **Network** → 点开 `/cgi-bin/assistant/qa` 这个请求 → **Request Headers**。 3. 把 **`x-ima-cookie`** 这个请求头的**整个值**复制下来，粘贴给 magpie。 > **必须是这个请求头的值，不能是浏览器的 cookie 存储。** ima 前端会往这个头里 > 放一些 cookie 存储里没有的字段，只用存储重建的 cookie 会被回 `600001 > 服务繁忙`。插件会提示你这一点，否则这个报错看起来像是 ima 在忙。 ### ima 桌面端登录 —— 已移除 曾经有过第二个登录方式，读 ima 桌面应用自己的 cookie 存储（用登录用户的 DPAPI 密钥解密）。**它不能用，已移除而不是作为一个必然失败的选项发出去。** 实测结论： - ima **从不把登录态写进磁盘**。Extension Cookies 里只有 ima 客户端组装的 11 个字段里的 5 个，而按 token 值（明文和 base64 两种形式）扫遍 profile 下 每个文件，零命中。登录态在进程内存里。 - 那 5 个字段是**上次退出登录前**的。重新登录只改写 `IMA-GUID`，两个 token 的 密文长度一字未变，ima 答 `code 41` / `110031 token session expired`。 - 拿完整的 11 个字段需要运行中客户端的 cookie，也就是要调试端口，而 `--remote-debugging-port` 现在无效。 所以这个选项只会失败，用户也看不出为什么失败。粘贴 cookie 是唯一可行的。 ## 使用 在 magpie 的 **设置 → 插件**，把下面任意一条粘进标着 *"已有想装的？"* 的输入框， 点**安装**： ``` github:dongsujiang0205-coder/magpie-ima-auth 从 GitHub D:\path\to\magpie-ima-auth 本机文件夹 magpie-ima-auth 从 npm（发布后） ``` 或者命令行。下面用 magpie 的可执行文件名 `magpie-windows-amd64.exe`（如果你 把它加进了 PATH，直接写 `magpie` 即可）： ```powershell & "D:\magpie-windows-amd64.exe" plugin add github:dongsujiang0205-coder/magpie-ima-auth & "D:\magpie-windows-amd64.exe" plugin login ima ``` `plugin login ima` 会打印上面的 cookie 步骤，然后等你粘贴。 OpenCode 用户在 `opencode.json` 里： ```json { "plugin": ["magpie-ima-auth"] } ``` 然后 `opencode auth login`。 ## 模型 登录后 magpie 里会看到： - **知识库模型**（8 个）：`deepseek-v4-flash`、`hy3` 等，ima 官方，免费。 - **Copilot 模型**（12 个，`copilot/` 开头）：消耗算力，每个模型倍率不同， 比如 `copilot/hy3` 是 ×0.2、`copilot/kimi-k3` 是 ×4.5。倍率显示在模型名里。 - **自定义模型**（你在 ima 里自己加的那些）：数量因账号而异。代码里没有硬编码， 每个用户只看到自己账号下的——不会出现在别人的列表里。 同名模型在两套目录里是不同的 ima 模型，所以 Copilot 的用 `copilot/` 前缀区分。 没登录时只显示前 8 个（静态表）。 ## 不支持 **工具调用（tools）。** ima 的问答接口一次只收一个字符串，没有工具通道。所有 模型都声明不支持工具。这是 ima 的限制，不是 bug——有其他插件用"把 schema 写进 prompt、解析打标签的回复"的方式模拟，但那依赖模型本来就没训过输出那些标签， 这里刻意没做。 **知识库定向。** ima 的问答跑在会话打开时绑定的知识库上，本插件开的是普通 会话，不是绑定某个知识库 id 的。 ## 每日签到（未实现） ima 每登录一天给 50 算力，领取接口是 `/cgi-bin/daily_login_activity/check_in`。**它无法从 ima 客户端之外调用**—— 以下都是在 app 自己标为可领的那天（`status: 3`、`button: "签到"`）实测的： - 路由确实存在：它回 403，而同前缀下其他名字（`claim_reward`、`share`、 `sign`、`reward` 等）全回 404。 - 所有请求体都被拒：`{}`、`reward_type` 0–20、`day`、`date`、`top`。 - 所有请求头组合都被拒：加/不加 `x-ima-uid`、`x-ima-token`、`sec-fetch-*`； 以及 `text/plain`、form-encoded、不带 Content-Type。 - 放在加密前缀 `/cgi-bin/s/` 下是 404。 - 调用它的代码不在 ima **1663 个扩展脚本**中的任何一个里，所以连请求体 长什么样都读不出来。 - 唯一能让请求加密的办法是客户端自己的调试端口，而 ima 已经不再开放： `--remote-debugging-port` 进了主进程命令行，但没有任何东西监听。 所以本插件**不导出** `auth.checkin`。否则 magpie 界面上会出现一个每天 都失败、用户也无从处理的「每日签到」——和下面那个桌面端登录是同一个道理。 读取签到状态仍然可以：`/cgi-bin/daily_login_activity/get_activity_info` 按天返回，每行带 `top`、`status`、`reward`，还有一个很有用的 `button`—— 它直接告诉你 app 会做什么（`签到` / `已领取` / `已过期`）。 ## 排查 | 现象 | 原因 | |---|---| | 登录时报 `600001 服务繁忙` | 粘贴的不是 `x-ima-cookie` 请求头的值，而是 cookie 存储 | | 登录时报 `41 登录过期` | cookie 是旧的，重新取一次 | | 模型列表只有 8 个 | 没登录。登录后会多出 copilot 模型和你自己的自定义模型 | | 没有 `copilot/` 开头的模型 | 没登录，或该账号的 Copilot 没开通 | | 用量卡显示算力但很慢 | ima 的接口慢，`get_balance` 是实时的 | | Agent 报工具错误 | 预期内，不支持工具 | ## 自查 ```sh npm test # 45 个测试，含对假服务器的一次端到端对话 node smoke.mjs # 10 项检查：magpie 调的每个钩子，形状按 magpie 源码 npm run scan # 这个仓库要发出去的东西里没有个人信息 ``` ## 发布 每次推送都是一个版本。`package.json` 里的版本号标记这次发布描述的状态， `v*` 标签标记代码是从哪个提交切出来的。 ```sh # 1. 定版本：修 bug 用 patch，加功能用 minor， # 插件与 magpie 的契约变了才用 major npm version patch # 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1（同时提交并打标签） # 2. 提交和标签一起推 git push origin main --tags # 3. 发到 npm npm publish ``` 标签比看起来重要：magpie 的 `magpie plugin update` 会装每个插件的最新版本， 而标签就是声明"最新版本对应哪个提交"。两个标签之间的提交属于开发过程—— 版本号只在切发布时才动，所以多个提交可以共用一个版本号。 GitHub 上也有发布页：**Releases → Create a new release** → 选刚推的标签。 ### 图标和简介从哪来 magpie 按**安装来源**取这两项，取的不是同一个地方： | 来源 | 图标 | 简介 | | --- | --- | --- | | npm 包 | `package.json` 的 `icon` | `package.json` 的 `description` | | 官方 marketplace | 随精选列表下发 | 随精选列表下发 | | GitHub 仓库 | 仓库 API 的 `icon` 字段 | 仓库的 Description | GitHub 的仓库 API 对**个人账号仓库不返回 `icon` 字段**，所以从 GitHub 安装时 卡片一定是通用图标。想要自己的图标，只能发 npm——这也是 `icon` 写成绝对 URL 并锁定到发布标签的原因：npm 那边要能直接取到图，相对路径 `icon.png` 解析不了。 GitHub 来源的简介只需在仓库页 About 旁边的齿轮里填 Description。 ## 许可 MIT。详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。
